correctness.rationale: In the real normalized Fourier basis of 1 constant plus r cosine/sine modes, demixed two-sensor samples have one constant column and r square 2×2 blocks. The raw time matrix is diag(V,V) times this demixed map, V the Vandermonde of distinct real spectral values. In the codimension-one rectangular case Cauchy–Binet/cofactor transport yields det(B*R*RB)=|det R|² det(B*B)||R^{-*}w||²; w is the sensor-block difference in the constant coordinate. Solving V^T a=e0 via the Lagrange cardinal polynomial gives the exact sum a_t², hence determinant factor (2/N)^(2r+1)(det V)^4(sum a_t²)∏sin²(2πkd/N). Rank is full iff N/gcd(N,2d)>r. For r=2, y=sin²θ gives 4y²(1−y), unique max y=2/3, so every discrete D-optimum belongs to floor(Mα),floor(Mα)+1; the algebraic-integer obstruction forbids reaching 16/27 on a finite rational grid. A global second derivative bound gives O(N^-2) and strict mismatch with demixed condition-optimum for 6|N,N≥42. Independent full raw Fourier-sample Gram comparisons matched 219 (N,r,d) cases; finite tests are corroboration, not proof.
